title: Invalid SSL certificate for picture of the day provider breaking screen locker
line: When a Picture of the Day site has a bad certificate, the lock screen keeps working instead of showing "the screen locker is broken".
explanation: Every Picture of the Day provider downloads with KIO::storedGet without the ssl_no_ui metadata, so when a site serves an invalid certificate KIO's http worker asks the user through a widget dialog. The lock screen greeter is a QGuiApplication, so creating that QWidget crashes it, KScreenLocker restarts it, it crashes again and the emergency 'screen locker is broken' screen appears (in System Settings the same dialog blocks the wallpaper page, bug 442912). All provider downloads now set ssl_no_ui, so a bad certificate just makes the download fail and the wallpaper falls back as for any other network error.

commits.message:
wallpapers/potd: don't ask about invalid certificates when downloading

When a provider's site served an invalid certificate, KIO asked about it
with a widget dialog, which crashed the lock screen greeter and blocked
the wallpaper settings page. Downloads now just fail in that case.

BUG: 526466
BUG: 442912

media.caption: Master: lock screen with Picture of the Day (NASA) while the site serves a self-signed certificate
With the fix: same setup, the greeter survives and shows the normal password prompt (no image)

reviews.text: Direct, well-placed fix setting KIO's ssl_no_ui metadata on all 15 KIO::storedGet jobs across all 6 Picture of the Day providers so invalid certificates fail cleanly instead of triggering a QWidget SSL dialog that crashes the QGuiApplication lock screen greeter (and blocks System Settings, bug 442912). Preserves PotdProvider ABI for clean backporting, and verification with both a self-signed certificate shim and a valid certificate proves the fix without regressions.

Correct root cause: the POTD providers' KIO::storedGet jobs let the http worker ask about bad certificates through a widget dialog, which kills the QGuiApplication greeter; setting ssl_no_ui on all 15 download call sites (every one in wallpapers/potd at the base) makes a bad certificate a plain download failure, which is exactly what the reporter expects ('continue running normally without displaying an image') and also removes the desktop-wallpaper popup the reporter mentions. Before/after screenshots show the 'screen locker is broken' screen replaced by a working password prompt, and the valid-certificate regression check passes. Nits: the 15 repeated addMetaData lines could be a small helper in the provider base, and the BUG: 442912 claim (System Settings wallpaper page) follows from the same change but was not exercised on the rig.
